description: Saved analyses whose stage layout left a hole, crowded a head or made a waiting piece travel (stage-layout work, October 2026). Entries named "-source-kept" are saved analyses with every movement hop rewritten so the lower occurrence keeps the source ID, as models write most hops (provenance names the saved analysis and the conversion). Kept outside fixtures/ so the fixture-wide audits do not take on their unrelated, pre-existing findings; tests/stageLayoutRegressions.test.mjs measures them on the corpus gate layout.

derivationStages.statement: The verb ראיתי merges with the resumptive pronoun אותו, forming VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The derivation starts inside the relative clause. The lexical verb ראיתי 'saw' externally merges with its internal argument, the accusative resumptive pronoun אותו 'him'. In this resumptive relative the pronoun occupies the ordinary object position where a gap would otherwise appear. The verb assigns the Theme role to the pronoun, so a theta relation links the verb to the resumptive. The verb is entered with its surface inflection; the past 1sg morphology is treated lexically, so no separate realization is needed.

derivationStages.statement: Light v merges, values accusative on the resumptive, attracts V, and introduces the null 1sg subject pro.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Transitive light v merges with VP. Its phi-probe finds the resumptive pronoun and values its case as accusative; this is recorded as an Agree relation between v and the resumptive. That case is overt in the form אותו, which is the accusative marker et fused with the 3sg.m clitic. The verb then head-moves and adjoins to v, the first step of Hebrew V-raising. The moved verb carries its pronunciation, and an unpronounced copy of the same lineage stays in VP. A head-movement relation links the moved verb, its lower copy and the v host. Finally the null subject pro, the 1sg agent licensed by the rich past-tense agreement of ראיתי, merges as the specifier of v. The v projection assigns it the Agent role, which is recorded as a theta relation.

derivationStages.statement: Past T merges, agrees with pro, attracts the V+v complex, and raises pro to its specifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Past-tense T merges with vP. Its unvalued phi-features probe and find pro, valuing T as 1sg and pro as nominative; this Agree relation links T and pro. The 1sg value matches the suffix of ראיתי and licenses the null subject. Next the V+v complex head-moves to T, completing Hebrew verb raising. A head-movement relation links the complex, its silent lower copy in the v position and the T host. Last, the EPP property of T attracts pro to the specifier of TP. Pro stays silent, and its lower copy remains in the specifier of v. An A-movement relation links the raised pro with that copy.

derivationStages.statement: The relative complementizer ש merges, and a base-generated null operator in its specifier binds the resumptive.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The invariant relative complementizer ש merges with the relative TP. It carries a relative feature that needs an operator specifier. Because the object position is filled by the resumptive אותו rather than a gap, nothing moves to the edge. Instead a null relative operator externally merges in the specifier of CP and satisfies the complementizer's relative feature, recorded as a feature-checking relation between the complementizer and the operator. The operator then A-bar-binds the resumptive pronoun at a distance. A binding relation links the operator to אותו and records the shared 3sg.m features. This base-generation-plus-binding analysis is what Hebrew resumption calls for.

derivationStages.statement: The head noun איש is introduced and the relative CP adjoins to it.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The head noun איש 'man' enters the derivation and the relative clause adjoins to it by pair-merge, the head-external analysis of the relative. The nominal projection keeps the noun's label, and the adjunction is recorded as a pair-merge relation between the noun host and the relative CP. Under adjunction the null operator is identified with the head noun, recorded as an identification relation between the operator and the noun. Through the operator's binding, the resumptive אותו is therefore interpreted as referring to the man.

derivationStages.statement: The definite article ה merges, forming the DP האיש שראיתי אותו.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The proclitic definite determiner ה merges with the modified nominal, yielding the definite DP 'the man that I saw (him)'. The article scopes over the whole noun-plus-relative, so it merges after the relative clause has adjoined. No relation beyond this construction step is established.

derivationStages.statement: A null Pred head takes the DP as predicate, and the demonstrative זה merges as its subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: For the copular clause, a silent Pred head merges with the definite DP, turning it into the nominal predicate. The demonstrative pronoun זה 'this' then merges in the specifier of Pred as the subject of predication. A predication relation links the demonstrative subject to its predicate. The clause is identificational: 'this is the man...'.

derivationStages.statement: Present T with a null copula merges, agrees with זה, and raises it to subject position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Matrix present-tense T merges with PredP. Hebrew present copular clauses need no overt copula, so T is unpronounced. T probes the demonstrative and values its own phi-features as 3sg.m while assigning nominative; an Agree relation links T and זה. The EPP property of T then raises the demonstrative to the specifier of TP. It is pronounced there, with a silent copy of the same lineage left in the specifier of Pred. An A-movement relation links the raised demonstrative with that copy.

derivationStages.statement: A null declarative C merges, completing the matrix clause זה האיש שראיתי אותו.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative complementizer merges with the matrix TP, typing the root clause as a declarative and closing the derivation. The pronounced terminals now read, in order: the demonstrative זה, the article ה, the noun איש, the complementizer ש, the raised verb ראיתי, and the resumptive אותו. Together they spell the input sentence. No further relation is established.

18.sentence: Ich glaube, dass der Arzt den Patienten nicht hätte operieren lassen dürfen.

derivationStages.statement: The lowest verb 'operieren' projects a head-final VP with its object 'den Patienten'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun 'Patienten' projects N-bar and NP, and the determiner 'den' sits in its specifier. In German the verb phrase is head-final, so this NP is merged to the left of 'operieren' as its complement. First, 'operieren' assigns its internal Theme role to 'den Patienten'. Second, the verb governs the NP and assigns it structural accusative Case. This is why the NP is accusative 'den' rather than nominative 'der'. Of the readings this string allows, the analysis takes the one where the patient is operated on, not the one where the patient operates. The agent of 'operieren' is left implicit.

derivationStages.statement: Causative 'lassen' takes the operieren-VP as its complement and 'der Arzt' as its external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'lassen' merges to the right of the operieren-VP, giving a head-final V-bar. First, causative 'lassen' c-selects a bare VP complement. That complement has no overt causee, which is the 'lassen'-passive pattern: the operating agent stays unexpressed. Next, the NP 'der Arzt' (determiner 'der' plus noun 'Arzt') is merged in the specifier of the lassen-VP, following the VP-internal subject hypothesis. There it receives the Causer (permitter) role from 'lassen'. It cannot get Case here, so it will later raise.

derivationStages.statement: Verb raising adjoins 'operieren' to 'lassen', forming the complex head 'operieren lassen'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Following Evers-style verb raising, the infinitive 'operieren' leaves its VP and left-adjoins to the governing verb 'lassen'. This forms a complex V that occupies the head position of the lassen-VP. A trace remains in the operieren-VP. The head-movement relation links the moved verb, its trace and its host. Left-adjunction gives the order 'operieren lassen', the ordinary descending cluster order in German.

derivationStages.statement: The deontic modal 'dürfen' takes the lassen-VP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'dürfen' merges to the right of the lassen-VP and projects V-bar and VP, with no specifier. It has no thematic subject of its own here: the Causer 'der Arzt' originates lower. The c-selection relation records that 'dürfen' selects a VP whose head is a bare infinitive. That status requirement is why 'lassen' surfaces as an infinitive.

derivationStages.statement: Verb raising adjoins 'operieren lassen' to 'dürfen'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex head 'operieren lassen' raises as a unit and left-adjoins to 'dürfen'. The result is the cluster 'operieren lassen dürfen' in the head position of the dürfen-VP. A trace remains in the head position of the lassen-VP. The head-movement relation connects the moved complex, its trace and the host 'dürfen'.

derivationStages.statement: Negation 'nicht' adjoins to the dürfen-VP and takes scope over the modal.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The adverb 'nicht' left-adjoins to the dürfen-VP, creating a new VP segment. The negation-scope relation records that 'nicht' c-commands the modal VP, giving the meaning 'not permitted'. The perfect auxiliary is not yet present, so the negation sits below it, as the reading 'should not have been allowed' requires.

derivationStages.statement: The perfect auxiliary 'hätte' selects the negated modal VP, triggering the Ersatzinfinitiv.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'hätte', the subjunctive-II form of the perfect auxiliary 'haben', merges to the right of the negated dürfen-VP and projects V-bar and VP. First, c-selection records that it takes this VP as its complement. Second, a perfect auxiliary normally governs a past participle, but a modal that itself governs a bare infinitive surfaces as an infinitive instead (infinitivus pro participio). The Ersatzinfinitiv relation records that 'dürfen' replaces expected 'gedurft' under 'hätte'.

derivationStages.statement: The cluster 'operieren lassen dürfen' raises to 'hätte' by right-adjunction (auxiliary flip).
derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex 'operieren lassen dürfen' raises to the auxiliary. Because the auxiliary governs an Ersatzinfinitiv, the cluster adjoins to the right of 'hätte' rather than the left. This is Oberfeldumstellung: the finite auxiliary precedes the infinitives in the order 'hätte operieren lassen dürfen'. A trace remains in the head of the dürfen-VP. The head-movement relation links the moved cluster, its trace and the host 'hätte', and records the reversed direction.

derivationStages.statement: The object 'den Patienten' scrambles out of its VP and adjoins to the hätte-VP, above the negation.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The surface order 'den Patienten nicht' shows that the object must precede the negation. So the object NP scrambles out of the operieren-VP and left-adjoins to the hätte-VP, creating a new VP segment. A trace remains in its base position. The scrambling relation forms the chain of the object, its trace and the VP it targets. Through this chain the object keeps the Theme role and accusative Case assigned at its base position.

derivationStages.statement: A head-final finite INFL takes the scrambled hätte-VP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A wordless finite INFL carrying tense and agreement merges to the right of the VP, because German IP is head-final. It projects I-bar and IP, and the IP specifier stays empty until the subject raises. The c-selection relation records that this finite INFL takes the VP complement.

derivationStages.statement: The verbal complex headed by 'hätte' moves to INFL.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The whole complex 'hätte operieren lassen dürfen' moves as a single head and left-adjoins to the empty INFL. A trace remains in the head of the hätte-VP. INFL is final, so the movement is string-vacuous. First, the head-movement relation links the complex, its trace and INFL. Second, a feature-checking relation records that INFL's finite features match the past subjunctive inflection of 'hätte'.

derivationStages.statement: The subject 'der Arzt' raises to Spec-IP, where it receives nominative Case and agrees with INFL.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'der Arzt' cannot receive Case inside the lassen-VP. It raises to the empty specifier of IP, leaving a trace in its theta position. First, the A-movement relation forms its chain. Second, finite INFL assigns nominative Case to the NP in its specifier, which is why it surfaces as 'der Arzt'. Third, an agreement relation between INFL and its specifier records third person singular, matching 'hätte'.

derivationStages.statement: The complementizer 'dass' heads the embedded CP and selects the finite IP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The overt complementizer 'dass' merges to the left of IP, because C is head-initial in German. It projects C-bar and CP. The c-selection relation records that 'dass' selects a finite declarative IP. Because 'dass' fills C, the finite verb cannot move to C, so the embedded clause stays verb-final.

derivationStages.statement: Matrix 'glaube' takes the dass-clause as complement and 'ich' as its external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb 'glaube' merges with the dass-CP to its left in the head-final VP. First, it assigns the Proposition role to that clause. Then the pronoun 'ich' (N projecting N-bar and NP) is merged in the specifier of VP, and 'glaube' assigns it the Experiencer role.

derivationStages.statement: The dass-clause extraposes and right-adjoins to the matrix VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A finite CP complement may not remain in the Case-marked preverbal position (Case Resistance). So the dass-clause moves rightward and right-adjoins to the matrix VP, creating a new VP segment. A trace remains in its base complement position. The extraposition relation records this chain and the VP it targets. As a result, the embedded clause follows the matrix verb, as the comma-separated surface order shows.

derivationStages.statement: A head-final finite matrix INFL takes the matrix VP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A wordless finite INFL merges to the right of the extended matrix VP and projects I-bar and IP, with the specifier still empty. The c-selection relation records that finite INFL takes the VP complement.

derivationStages.statement: Matrix 'glaube' moves to INFL.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite verb 'glaube' left-adjoins to the matrix INFL, leaving a trace in the VP head. The head-movement relation links the verb, its trace and INFL. This first step of verb movement feeds the later move to C.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix subject 'ich' raises to Spec-IP for nominative Case and agreement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'ich' raises from the specifier of VP to the specifier of the matrix IP, leaving a trace. First, the A-movement relation forms the chain. Second, finite INFL assigns nominative Case to it. Third, the agreement relation between INFL and its specifier records first person singular, matching 'glaube'.

derivationStages.statement: An empty matrix C selects the finite IP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The root clause has no overt complementizer, so a wordless C merges to the left of IP and projects C-bar and CP. The c-selection relation records that this root C takes a finite IP and carries the verb-second property, so it attracts the finite verb.

derivationStages.statement: The finite verb moves from INFL to C (verb second).
derivationStages.stageRecord: The INFL complex containing 'glaube' moves to the empty root C and left-adjoins to it, leaving a trace in INFL. The head-movement relation records this I-to-C step, which places the finite verb in second position.

derivationStages.statement: The subject 'ich' moves to Spec-CP, completing the verb-second main clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb-second clause needs one constituent before the finite verb in C. The subject 'ich' moves from the specifier of IP to the specifier of CP, leaving a second trace. The A-bar-movement relation forms this step of its chain. The result is the full sentence 'Ich glaube, dass der Arzt den Patienten nicht hätte operieren lassen dürfen'.

21.sentence: Atzo liburutegian ikusi nuen gizonak esan dit liburu hori ez duela inoiz irakurri.

derivationStages.statement: The embedded verb phrase 'liburu hori irakurri' is built.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun 'liburu' merges with the demonstrative 'hori'. The demonstrative is the determiner and follows its nominal, as Basque determiners do, so the object is 'liburu hori'. This object then merges as the complement of the participle 'irakurri' ('read'), which is head-final in Basque. In that position the verb assigns the Theme role to 'liburu hori'.

derivationStages.statement: The embedded vP is completed with a null ergative subject and the adverb 'inoiz'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges to the right of the verb phrase. A null third-person pronoun merges at its edge as the reader and receives the Agent role from the light verb. This pronoun is the unexpressed subject of 'duela', the one who has never read the book. The adverb 'inoiz' ('ever') then adjoins to the left of this vP. It is a temporal modifier, not an argument, and the adjunction relation records that status.

derivationStages.statement: The embedded auxiliary 'du' merges as T and agrees with both arguments.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite auxiliary 'du' merges as a head-final T above the vP. Basque auxiliaries index more than one argument, so T probes twice. It first agrees with the null subject, valuing ergative case and a third-singular feature that the form spells as zero. It then agrees with 'liburu hori', valuing absolutive case and third singular, which surfaces as the initial 'd-' of 'du'.

derivationStages.statement: Negation 'ez' heads a left-headed polarity phrase, licenses 'inoiz', and attracts the auxiliary.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The negative head 'ez' merges above the TP as a left-headed polarity head. Once merged, it c-commands 'inoiz' and licenses it, since 'inoiz' is a negative polarity item that needs negation here. The auxiliary 'du' then raises from T and adjoins to the right of 'ez', forming the complex head 'ez du'. A silent copy stays in T. This head movement is why the auxiliary precedes the vP material 'inoiz irakurri' in this negative clause.

derivationStages.statement: The complementizer '-ela' merges, attracts 'ez du', and the object 'liburu hori' is topicalized to the clause edge.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The declarative subordinating complementizer '-ela' merges above the polarity phrase. The complex head 'ez du' raises and attaches to its left, so the three pieces form one complex head spelled 'ez duela'. A silent copy of 'ez du' stays in the polarity head. Next the object 'liburu hori' undergoes A-bar movement to the specifier of this complementizer as a topic, leaving a silent copy in object position. This is why the object is pronounced before the negated auxiliary.

derivationStages.statement: A separate relative-clause verb phrase with a null operator object is built.
derivationStages.stageRecord: In a separate part of the workspace, the relative clause begins. A silent relative operator merges as the object of 'ikusi' ('see') and receives the Theme role. This gap position is the one the head noun 'gizon' will be understood to fill. The finished embedded clause stays in the workspace as an independent object.

derivationStages.statement: The relative-clause vP receives a first-person null subject and the adjuncts 'liburutegian' and 'atzo'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges, and a null first-singular pronoun merges at its edge as the seer, receiving the Agent role. The locative phrase 'liburutegian' is then built from 'liburutegi' and the inessive postposition '-an', and adjoins to the vP. Next 'atzo' ('yesterday') adjoins outside it. Both modifiers belong inside the relative clause. The matrix verb 'esan dit' is a present perfect of the recent past, which does not combine naturally with 'atzo', so the seeing happened yesterday. Adjoining 'atzo' outermost makes it the leftmost word of the clause.

derivationStages.statement: Past auxiliary 'nuen' agrees with both arguments, the relative C merges, and the operator moves to its edge.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The past auxiliary 'nuen' merges as T. It first agrees with the first-singular subject, valuing ergative case, which its prefix 'n-' spells. It then agrees with the operator object, valuing absolutive third singular. Next the relative complementizer '-n' merges. It has no separate spelling, because after a past form already ending in '-n' the relative suffix is absorbed. Finally the relative complementizer attracts the operator to its specifier, leaving a silent copy in object position.

derivationStages.statement: The relative clause merges with the head noun 'gizon', and the article '-a' and ergative '-k' complete 'gizonak'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finished relative clause merges to the left of the head noun 'gizon', as Basque relatives are prenominal. The relative operator is then identified with this head noun, so the noun is interpreted as the one seen yesterday in the library. The article '-a' then merges as the determiner, and the ergative case marker '-k' merges above it as K. Together they spell 'gizonak'.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix verb 'esan' takes the embedded clause and a null first-person dative.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb 'esan' ('say, tell') merges with the embedded clause 'liburu hori ez duela inoiz irakurri' and assigns it the Theme role as the content of the telling. A null first-singular pronoun then merges as the addressee in the higher verbal position and receives the Goal role. This pronoun is the 'me' indexed by the auxiliary 'dit'.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix light verb merges and 'gizonak' becomes the external argument, the antecedent of the embedded null subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges above the matrix verb phrase. The ergative phrase headed by 'gizon' merges at its edge and receives the Agent role, as the man who told. Now that both are in one tree, this phrase serves as the antecedent of the null subject of 'duela'. The man is therefore the one who has never read that book.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix auxiliary 'dit' merges as T and agrees with three arguments.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The ditransitive present auxiliary 'dit' merges as T and agrees three times, in order. First it agrees with 'gizonak', valuing ergative third singular, which is spelled as zero. Second it agrees with the null addressee, valuing dative first singular, spelled '-t'. Third it agrees with the clausal complement, which carries the default third-singular absolutive value, spelled 'd-'.

derivationStages.statement: The finite complement clause extraposes to the right, and the matrix declarative C closes the sentence.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite clause 'liburu hori ez duela inoiz irakurri' extraposes rightward and adjoins to the matrix TP, leaving a silent copy in its complement position. As in usual Basque practice for finite complements, the clause is therefore pronounced after 'esan dit', not before the verb. Finally a silent declarative complementizer merges and completes the sentence.

27.sentence: Juan quiere que se lo expliquemos a su hermana antes de que ella decida vender la casa.

derivationStages.statement: Construct the argument structure and the independent temporal phrase for the embedded-attachment reading.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Build the main clause and its finite complement, leaving the temporal phrase separate until its attachment is established. Querer assigns Juan the experiencer role and the que-clause the desired-proposition role. Explicar assigns the silent first-person-plural subject the agent role, its null pronominal object the theme role, and a su hermana the recipient role. The two selected internal complements are sisters of explicar within V′. Decidir assigns ella the decider role and its infinitival complement the content role; vender assigns PRO the agent role and la casa the theme role. Adopt a base-generated clitic analysis: dative le is linked to the overt recipient phrase, while accusative lo licenses the null thematic object. Thus the clitics do not introduce additional thematic arguments. Ella controls the infinitival PRO. Querer selects the subjunctive finite complement; the complex temporal preposition antes de selects a finite que-clause with subjunctive decida; decidir selects the nonfinite complement containing vender. Subjects occupy Spec-IP, and the finite and infinitival verbs are initially in their lexical V positions. Their lexical forms already carry the inflection that will be licensed under I.

values.dependency: The dative clitic and the overt recipient realize one recipient dependency.

derivationStages.statement: Raise the verbs to I, license Case and null subjects, and derive the clitic sequence se lo.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First raise quiere from the main V position to its finite I, leaving a head trace. Next raise expliquemos to the inflectional head below the two clitics, preserving their dative–accusative order. Then raise decida to the temporal clause's finite I and vender to infinitival I, each leaving its own head trace. The four movements are local V-to-I movements and do not cross a clause boundary. With the finite heads established, their agreement licenses nominative Juan, first-person-plural pro, and ella; first-person-plural agreement identifies the null explaining subject. The object chains receive accusative from explicar and vender, while a assigns the recipient NP oblique Case. PRO remains Caseless and ungoverned in the nonfinite subject position, as required by the GB PRO analysis adopted here. Finally, realize the dative clitic le as se before the third-person accusative clitic lo. This is contextual allomorphy, not reflexivization, and neither clitic moves in this analysis.

derivationStages.statement: Attach the temporal phrase to the explaining VP and complete the embedded-attachment reading.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Right-adjoin antes de que ella decida vender la casa to the embedded explaining VP. This combines the previously independent temporal phrase with the main tree and places the before-relation inside the proposition Juan wants: the desired explanation to the sister is to precede her decision to sell the house. The temporal phrase does not assert that Juan's wanting itself precedes that decision. The pronominal dependencies remain distinct from attachment: se is dative rather than a reflexive subject anaphor; su has no grammatically obligatory possessor antecedent; and ella is free in its local finite clause. Ella can refer to the sister or another contextually salient feminine singular individual, and su can refer to Juan or another suitable third-person possessor without requiring a different constituent structure.

values.interpretation: Juan wants us to explain it to his/her/their sister before she decides to sell the house.

values.dative_status: clitic doubling, not a Principle A anaphor
values.possessive_reference: not obligatorily fixed by the syntax
values.subject_reference: free in its local domain; compatible with reference to the sister or another salient feminine singular referent

30.sentence: 太郎は花子が昨日図書館で借りた本を次郎がもう読んだと思っている。

derivationStages.statement: The relative-clause verb 借り merges with a null pronominal object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative clause is built first, since it is the most deeply embedded part of the object. Japanese prenominal relatives show no island effects. I therefore treat the gap not as a moved operator but as a null pronominal object (pro), which external Merge combines with the verb 借り. The verb assigns the Theme role to this pro, so pro is what was borrowed. That relation is recorded here.

derivationStages.statement: The locative phrase 図書館で is built and adjoined to the relative-clause VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The postposition で merges with the noun 図書館 in a separate step. Because で is head-final, the result is the postpositional phrase 図書館で. This phrase is a location modifier, not an argument of 借り. It therefore attaches to the VP by adjunction, which leaves the VP label unchanged. The adjunction relation links the locative phrase to the VP of 借り.

derivationStages.statement: Silent v merges with the relative-clause VP, and 花子が is merged as its external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges with the VP that already contains the locative adjunct. Separately, the name 花子 merges with the case particle が to form a case phrase. That phrase is then externally merged at the edge of the light-verb phrase. The light verb assigns the Agent role to 花子が, making Hanako the borrower.

derivationStages.statement: The temporal adverb 昨日 adjoins to the relative-clause vP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 昨日 modifies the borrowing event as a whole. It therefore adjoins to the vP above the base position of 花子が. When the subject later raises, this adverb will follow 花子が on the surface. The adjunction relation links 昨日 to the vP.

derivationStages.statement: The past tense た merges, and its tense head agrees with 花子が.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The past-tense head た merges to the right of the vP, following Japanese head-final order. This tense head then probes into the vP and agrees with the subject case phrase 花子が, giving it nominative case, which が spells out. The Agree relation connects the tense head to 花子が while 花子が is still in its base position.

derivationStages.statement: 花子が raises to the specifier of the relative-clause TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The tense head's EPP property attracts 花子が. Internal Merge places it at the edge of the TP, giving the order 花子が 昨日 図書館で 借りた. The moved phrase is pronounced only at the landing site. At its base position at the edge of the light-verb phrase, an unpronounced lower occurrence remains, sharing its identity with the moved phrase. The movement relation connects the mover, its lower occurrence and the new TP.

derivationStages.statement: The relative TP adjoins to the head noun 本, and the null gap is identified with 本.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun 本 enters the derivation. The finished relative TP, which has no overt complementizer, adjoins to the left of it, so the noun keeps its label. Within this adjunction, the null object pro of 借り is then identified with the head noun, which yields the reading 'the book that Hanako borrowed'. Two relations are recorded in that order: the relative adjoins to 本, and pro is coindexed with 本.

derivationStages.statement: The case particle を merges with the modified noun, forming the object case phrase.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The accusative particle を merges to the right of the relative-modified noun. The result is the case phrase 花子が昨日図書館で借りた本を, which will be the object of 読ん. Its case is valued only later, by the light verb of the embedded clause, so no relation is recorded in this stage.

derivationStages.statement: The embedded verb 読ん merges with the object case phrase.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded clause begins when the verb 読ん merges with the object case phrase. The verb assigns the Theme role to that phrase, which is the thing read. The case phrase's base position therefore lies inside the embedded VP, even though it surfaces before 次郎が.

derivationStages.statement: Silent v merges, agrees with the object, and takes 次郎が as its external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First, a silent light verb merges with the VP of 読ん. It probes its complement and agrees with the object case phrase, valuing accusative case, which を spells out. Next, 次郎 combines with が, and the result is externally merged at the edge of the light-verb phrase. There the light verb assigns it the Agent role. The two relations follow this order: accusative Agree with the object, then the Agent role for 次郎が.

derivationStages.statement: The object moves to the outer edge of the embedded vP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The object will later appear in front of 次郎が. The light-verb phrase is a phase, and its VP complement becomes inaccessible once the phase is complete. The object therefore first moves to an outer edge position of the light-verb phrase, outside 次郎が. An unpronounced lower occurrence remains inside the VP. The movement relation connects the object, its VP-internal lower occurrence and the extended light-verb phrase.

derivationStages.statement: The aspectual adverb もう adjoins to the embedded vP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: もう ('already') modifies the reading event. It adjoins to the light-verb phrase, so it ends up below the surface position of 次郎が but before the verb. The adjunction relation links もう to the light-verb phrase.

derivationStages.statement: The past tense だ merges and agrees with 次郎が.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded past-tense head merges in head-final position. After the nasal-stem verb 読ん, it surfaces as だ. It probes and agrees with 次郎が in its base position, valuing nominative case, which が spells out. The Agree relation connects this tense head to 次郎が.

derivationStages.statement: 次郎が raises to the specifier of the embedded TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The EPP property of the embedded tense head attracts 次郎が. It moves from its base position at the edge of the light-verb phrase to the edge of TP, so it now precedes もう. An unpronounced lower occurrence remains at its base position. The movement relation connects 次郎が, that lower occurrence and the new TP.

derivationStages.statement: The object scrambles from the vP edge to a TP-adjoined position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The object case phrase is still at the edge of the light-verb phrase. It now undergoes clause-internal scrambling and adjoins to the embedded TP. This puts 花子が昨日図書館で借りた本を before 次郎が. The scrambling is treated as clause-internal because no matrix element intervenes between it and the embedded clause. A second unpronounced lower occurrence remains at the edge of the light-verb phrase. The scrambling relation connects the object, that lower occurrence and the TP-adjoined projection.

derivationStages.statement: The quotative complementizer と merges with the embedded TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The quotative complementizer と merges to the right of the embedded TP and closes off the finite complement clause that 思う selects. No new relation arises in this stage. The selection by the matrix verb is recorded when that verb merges.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix verb 思っ merges with the と-clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb stem 思っ merges with the complement clause headed by と. It selects that clause and assigns it the Proposition role, the content of the thinking. The relation links the verb to the clause.

derivationStages.statement: Matrix silent v merges, and 太郎は is merged as its external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent matrix light verb merges with the VP of 思っ. Separately, 太郎 combines with a topic-marked case particle spelled は. The resulting phrase is externally merged at the edge of the light-verb phrase, where the light verb assigns it the Experiencer role as the thinker.

derivationStages.statement: The aspect head てい and the nonpast tense る merge, and the tense head agrees with 太郎は.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The aspect head てい, the progressive/resultative form te-i, merges above the light-verb phrase. The nonpast tense head る then merges above the aspect phrase, completing 思っている. The tense head agrees with 太郎は at its base position and values nominative case. Because the case phrase also bears a topic feature, the case particle is spelled は rather than が. The Agree relation links the matrix tense head to 太郎は.

derivationStages.statement: 太郎は raises to the specifier of the matrix TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The EPP property of the matrix tense head attracts 太郎は from the edge of the matrix light-verb phrase to the edge of TP. An unpronounced lower occurrence remains in the light-verb phrase. The movement relation connects 太郎は, that lower occurrence and the matrix TP.

derivationStages.statement: A silent Top head merges, and 太郎は moves to its specifier, completing the sentence.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent, head-final topic head merges with the matrix TP. Its topic feature attracts the は-marked phrase 太郎は from the edge of TP, so 太郎は ends up sentence-initially as a thematic topic. A further unpronounced lower occurrence remains in the TP. The relation records this topicalizing movement, connecting 太郎は, its TP-level lower occurrence and the topic projection. The pronounced terminals now spell out the whole sentence in order.

32.sentence: நேற்று நூலகத்தில் நான் பார்த்த புத்தகத்தை என் தம்பி ஏற்கனவே படித்துவிட்டான்.

derivationStages.statement: Reading 1: both நேற்று ‘yesterday’ and நூலகத்தில் ‘in the library’ modify the seeing event inside the relative clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The participial clause is initially built with நான் as its overt nominative subject and a silent relative operator in the direct-object position of பார்த்த. The seeing predicate assigns Agent to நான் and Theme to that operator. Participial INFL licenses the overt nominative subject; this is not a PRO-subject clause. The silent locative P licenses the locative nominal நூலகத்தில், whose suffix is retained within the inflected noun. The locative phrase modifies the seeing event, and நேற்று supplies that event's time. In the separate matrix clause, finite INFL licenses என் தம்பி as nominative Agent and bears past, third-person singular masculine features. The genitive pronoun என் is the possessor of தம்பி. ஏற்கனவே modifies the matrix reading event. The matrix verb's object position remains unfilled until the headed relative nominal is assembled. The inflected verbal words are retained whole on their lexical heads; abstract INFL heads do not introduce additional pronounced material.

values.interpretation: the seeing takes place in the library
the completed reading holds already at the relevant reference time

derivationStages.statement: The participial relative is completed and the resulting book nominal enters the matrix object position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First, பார்த்த raises from its established V position to participial INFL, leaving a verbal trace. Its whole-word pronunciation is retained at the raised occurrence. Next, the silent relative operator moves from the established object position to Spec-CP, leaving an A′-trace; the operator binds that trace. The resulting head-final CP adjoins to the noun's N′. The external head புத்தகத்தை is coindexed with the operator chain, giving the restrictive interpretation ‘book which I saw yesterday in the library’. The complete nominal is then inserted as the complement of the matrix reading predicate. That predicate assigns it Theme and accusative Case, overtly reflected in புத்தகத்தை. Both the matrix verb and the newly integrated object remain in their matrix base positions at this stage.

values.interpretation: book that the speaker saw yesterday in the library

derivationStages.statement: Matrix verb raising and object scrambling produce the completed sentence under the relative-clause attachment reading.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verbal complex raises from V to finite INFL, leaving a head trace and licensing its past and third-person singular masculine inflection. Next, the entire accusative nominal moves from the previously established matrix complement position to an IP-adjoined position preceding என் தம்பி. Its source is an A′-trace, so the surface object–subject order is derived by scrambling rather than by generating the object outside the predicate's Case and theta domain. The relative clause travels inside that nominal; no extraction crosses the relative-clause boundary. A silent declarative C closes the matrix clause. Finally, நான் and என் are identified as independently referring to the speaker: neither locally binds the other, so their shared reference does not violate Principle B. The pronounced yield is exactly the input sentence.

values.bindingStatus: independent reference; no local pronominal binding

c1-007-source-kept.sentence: 他把那封信寄给了老师。

derivationStages.statement: 建立“寄给”的双层VP及其内部论元。
derivationStages.stageRecord: 采用双层VP分析：“寄”表达寄送方式，选择以“给”为中心的转移结构；这不是把句子分析成两个独立事件。先建立“寄”对下层VP的选择关系，再由下层“给”向其指定语“那封信”指派Theme角色，向补足语“老师”指派Goal/Recipient角色，最后由“给”许可接收者的内在与格。“那封信”内部以“那”为D，以“封”为量词中心语，以“信”为名词中心语；“老师”是带空D的名词短语。Theme的结构格尚待“把”结构许可。

values.selection: 寄 selects a transfer VP headed by 给

derivationStages.statement: “给”移至“寄”，形成复合动词中心语“寄给”。
derivationStages.stageRecord: 下层动词“给”从已经建立的下层V位置移至上层“寄”，在“寄”的右侧附加，形成一个复合V中心语。移动在原位置留下无声的动词语迹；“给”与该语迹构成中心语链，接收者仍处于下层动词的补足语位置，原有题元关系和与格许可由此保留。这里明确选择“寄给”作为单一寄送—转移谓词的复合动词分析。

values.chain: head chain preserving lower argument licensing

derivationStages.statement: 建立主语、把字结构和完成体投射。
derivationStages.stageRecord: 在现有VP之上依次建立AspP、AgrOP、BaP和IP。Asp中心语“了”选择寄送事件；AgrOP提供本分析中把字宾语的派生位置，其指定语暂空；“把”选择该宾语许可投射。主语“他”直接生成于Spec-IP，采用GB中外部论元位于VP之外的分析，不另设主语从VP移出的步骤。首先由寄送谓词向“他”指派Agent角色，其次由无声I许可主语的主格，最后建立“了”对整个寄送VP的完成体作用域。无声I不表示汉语具有英语式的显性时态或一致形态。

derivationStages.statement: 复合动词提升至Asp，得到“寄给了”的中心语次序。
derivationStages.stageRecord: 已形成的复合V“寄给”从上层V位置移至紧邻的Asp中心语，并左附加于“了”，使复合中心语内部的发音次序成为“寄—给—了”。原上层V位置留下无声语迹；“寄给”与该语迹建立V到Asp的中心语链，下层“给”的语迹继续保留。因此“了”是动词后的完成体标记，而不是句末语气词。此时Theme仍在下层VP的原始位置，尚未形成最终把字宾语次序。

derivationStages.statement: Theme移至把字宾语位置，完成“他把那封信寄给了老师”。
derivationStages.stageRecord: “那封信”从已经建立的下层Spec-VP移至Spec-AgrOP，在原位置留下无声DP语迹；这是不新增题元角色的A移位，其链在原位置获得Theme解释。随后“把”通过其选择的AgrOP宾语许可域，向该指定语中的“那封信”许可结构宾格；这里采用把字结构包含AgrOP的GB实现，而不把“把”分析为另一个给主语指派题元角色的实义动词。最后，移出的DP局部约束其原位语迹，形成满足空语类要求的论元链。“他”和“老师”均未移动；“老师”的接收者角色及内在与格保持不变。最终有声叶节点依次为“他、把、那、封、信、寄、给、了、老师”，与输入完全对应。
